text:
emma: FYI several customers hit restore failures after today's RBAC prune. Error shows KMS decrypt denied when unwrapping DEKs.
rishi: which key / snapshot? paste minimal log
emma: snapshot=db-snap-20260305 tenant=gamma
```
2026-04-12T11:04:02Z ERROR restore: dek_unwrap: rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = caller lacks cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
2026-04-12T11:04:02Z INFO snapshot=db-snap-20260305 restore_id=rs-421
```
sgt-bot: IAM audit: removed group binding `group:legacy-uploaders@redwood.com` from multiple SAs at 2026-04-12T10:30:00Z
claire: looks like uploader service accounts lost KMS decrypt via that group. The key is HSM-backed (customer-managed) and its IAM only listed the group for decrypt.
emma: customer impacted. we need a short-term fix and a long-term design. Immediate option: grant decrypt to the specific uploader SA temporarily. Long-term: don't let uploaders talk to KMS decrypt directly.
rishi: propose a "kms-delegate-proxy" internal service that holds decrypt rights and exposes a narrow RPC: RewrapDEK(requester_sa, snapshot_id) -> returns rewrapped DEK for restore. That way we keep KMS grants on the proxy SA and remove decrypt from many SAs.
olga: agree. Also propose conditional key IAM binding as a stopgap: add binding with condition restricting decrypt to requests where `request.auth.claims.email` equals uploader SA and `resource.name` matches the backup cryptoKey. That lowers blast radius.
claire: sample condition we tested in staging (pseudo):
```
bindings:
- role: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
  members: ["serviceAccount:uploader@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"]
  condition: "request.time < timestamp('2026-04-12T13:00:00Z') && request.auth.claims.email == 'uploader@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com'"
```
We simulated with `gcloud kms keys test-iam-permissions` and the deny matched earlier.
emma: I applied a temporary conditional binding for the affected uploader SA with a 2 hour TTL and re-ran the restore: success.
rishi: action items:
- (SEC) inventory all pipelines where uploader SAs call KMS decrypt directly and add to ENGSEC ticket 7882. owner: emma.
- (ENG) design & implement kms-delegate-proxy microservice, run under `backup-decryptor@redwood-prod` SA with KMS decrypt on relevant keys. owner: rishi.
- (SRE) add a pre-merge RBAC check and CI smoke: after RBAC PR, run `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy` for backups keyring and run a tiny restore smoke to verify unwrap. owner: olga.
- (SEC) add low-noise alert on KMS key IAM removals for backups keyRing and create a playbook entry for temporary conditional grants. owner: claire.
- (ENG/SEC) look into legacy snapshots encrypted with old DEK format; rewrap migration may be required. owner: rishi.
claire: also adding terraform pre-commit hook to run a policy check: ensure no PRs remove `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` from known-decrypt SAs without a replacement mapping.
emma: I'll notify affected customers with timeline and mitigation note. revoking temp grant in 1.5 hours.
olga: CI smoke passed after temp grant: https://ci.internal/restore/smoke/3961023456
rishi: for the proxy design, keep the API minimal, audit all calls, and include rate limits + mTLS. We'll include signed audit tokens so key policy can be tightened to accept requests only from the proxy SA.
emma: thanks all. filing ENGSEC-7882 and linking this thread. :thumbsup:
note: Slack thread stored as one continuous string. No title field included per agents.md.
